items.q: A part that measures something in the world, like light or soil moisture, is a…
Giving up one good thing to get another, like battery life for wireless, is a…
Users keep pressing the wrong button on a gadget because two buttons look the same. Best recommendation?
choices: print smaller labels on both buttons
move both buttons to the back
ask users to be more careful
give the two buttons different shapes

items.q: A plant-watering gadget needs to know if soil is dry. Which part?
items.why: A moisture sensor measures how wet the soil is. A speaker, a screen or a battery cannot tell if the soil is dry.

items.q: A wireless sensor vs a cable: the tradeoff is…
items.why: Wireless lets the sensor move freely, but it uses more battery than a cable. You get one good thing and give up another.

items.q: Users say the gadget's text is too small outdoors. Best improvement?
items.why: The users said the text is too small outdoors, so the next improvement is bigger, brighter text. Users decide what is next.

items.q: Replacing a part with one you know works, to find the fault, is a…
The printer prints from one laptop but not from the other. Where is the fault most likely?
choices: the printer, since it is the shared part
the paper tray, since both laptops use it
the building's power, since both plug into it
the laptop that cannot print, or its connection
items.why: The printer works from one laptop, so the printer is fine. The fault moves with the laptop that fails, or its connection.

items.q: What does "change one thing at a time" do for troubleshooting?
items.why: Change one thing, then test. If it works, you know exactly which change fixed it; change three at once and you cannot tell.

items.q: "Is it plugged in?" or "replace the main board": which check comes first, and why?
choices: replace the board, because it is thorough
is it plugged in, because it is cheap and quick
items.why: Cheap, quick checks come before slow, expensive ones. Checking the plug takes seconds; replacing a board costs time and money.

items.q: Showing the same data in a different form, like binary or RGB, is a different…

items.why: The places are worth 8, 4, 2 and 1. 1010 has the 8 and the 2 switched on: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Which three numbers make pure red in RGB?
items.why: RGB means red, green, blue. Pure red is red full on and the other two off: 255, 0, 0.

items.q: How many different colors can 2 bits per pixel show?
items.why: One bit shows 2 values, and each extra bit doubles that. 2 bits give 2 x 2 = 4 different colors.
